q: The toric code (Kitaev 1997) is a quantum error correcting code whose decoding is equivalent to:
opts: A 2D classical statistical mechanics problem (random-bond Ising model) — errors are anyons that must be pair-annihilated
Solving a system of linear equations
exp: The toric code on a torus: errors create 'anyon' excitations (violations of vertex/plaquette stabilizers). Error correction = bringing anyons together to annihilate them. The threshold theorem for the toric code corresponds to a phase transition in the 2D random-bond Ising model.
